findings.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts the try/catch wraps synchronous forEach over fire-and-forget async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls, so the catch is dead code and rejections become unhandled promise rejections

In workflows.tsx the async callback inside remindersToUpdate.forEach is not awaited, so the mutation proceeds before deletes complete, causing rescheduling while old reminders are still being deleted with no error surfaced

Changing deleteMany to delete in emailReminderManager.ts/smsReminderManager.ts throws P2025 on double invocation (cancelled-then-rescheduled bookings flow through both handlers), causing the subsequent SendGrid/Twilio cancel to silently fail and reminders to stay live
The event-type disable path in workflows.tsx removed ownership scoping (userId check) from reminder deletion, allowing users to cancel and delete other users' scheduled reminders

The sweep in scheduleEmailReminders.ts doesn't check scheduled or referenceId, so a cancelled reminder with null referenceId issues a SendGrid request with null batch_id that fails, aborting deletion of that reminder and all subsequent ones since Promise.all never runs
WorkflowStepContainer.tsx removed the isSenderIdNeeded render branch but kept the variable, losing the sender-ID input so SMS workflow steps can't be completed and possibly failing lint

In handleCancelBooking.ts reminder deletes are fired un-awaited, so the cancel response returns before cancellation completes, exposing stale cancelled:false rows and risking half-cancelled DB state with no rollback

Reschedule path cancels SendGrid sends but orphans WorkflowReminder DB rows: immediateDelete=true branch returns early after the SendGrid cancel POST without deleting or flagging the DB row, leaving rows with scheduled:true and cancelled:null that the cron (which only queries cancelled:true) never reaps, leaking phantom active reminders for superseded bookings
Diff contains zero tests for any of the new cancellation semantics (immediate SendGrid cancel, deferred cancelled:true + cron sweep, SMS hard delete, new DB column, new cron branch)

Cron cancel branch error handling: if a SendGrid cancel call fails mid-loop, console.log swallows the error and the already-computed deletes are skipped, leaving reminders cancelled:true forever with no retry or cleanup

Cron cancel branch in scheduleEmailReminders.ts doesn't filter on method: it selects all cancelled reminders regardless of method and unconditionally calls the SendGrid cancel endpoint, so a non-email reminder gets a bogus SendGrid cancel and its row is deleted without cancelling the SMS, causing the Twilio SMS to still fire

Reschedule path has no handling for reschedule failure: old booking's reminders are cancelled before eventManager.reschedule runs, so if rescheduling throws, the attendee keeps the old time slot but receives no reminders with no rollback or post-success guard

workflows.tsx uses fire-and-forget forEach(async ...) deletions that race with subsequent writes, so the next scheduleWorkflowReminders can run while old reminders are still being cancelled, intermittently leaving stale scheduled reminders that send for removed workflows

handleCancelBooking.ts dropped the .scheduled/.referenceId guard: any WorkflowMethods enum value other than EMAIL and SMS matches neither manager branch, so its cancelled-booking reminder rows are never deleted and accumulate
Mass re-indentation of the sendTestReminder/preview handler in workflows.tsx (~923-990) with no semantic change inflates the diff and makes real behavioral changes unreviewable

WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 changes wrapper condition from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, silently removing sender-ID panel rendering — an unscoped user-visible behavior change

scheduleEmailReminders.ts sweeps all cancelled:true reminders globally with no user or method filter, giving email a soft-cancel lifecycle while deleteScheduledSMSReminder (smsReminderManager.ts:177) hard-deletes rows immediately — undeclared asymmetric design across transports

Call sites (handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking) must know which cancellation semantics to invoke, e.g. immediateDelete is only ever passed for email, baking transport-specific policy into cross-cutting call sites
immediateDelete third parameter on deleteScheduledEmailReminder leaks call-site-specific policy into a shared manager, giving it contradictory semantics with no documented requirement mapping
handleNewBooking.ts:965 uses immediateDelete: true for email but the paired SMS call has no equivalent — same lifecycle event gets opposite persistence semantics per transport

workflows.tsx:572-580 deletion moved into shared managers that delete by bare id with no ownership check, losing the user-scoping clause (booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }) and introducing an authorization regression
schema.prisma cancelled Boolean? column is nullable with no default and no code writes false, introducing a NULL third state that future queries like cancelled: false will silently miss

Fire-and-forget deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls in handleCancelBooking.ts (and bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) are un-awaited inside forEach with the previous Promise.all guarantee removed, so cancellation never completes in serverless environments, causing cancelled bookings to still send reminders and reminder rows to leak

deleteScheduledEmailReminder swallows all errors with console.log and returns normally, so combined with un-awaited calls there is no path to detect failed SendGrid cancels, meaning reminders for every cancelled booking are sent forever with no signal

Sequential per-reminder SendGrid API calls in scheduleEmailReminders.ts cron loop cause N+1 external calls, and a single try/catch around the loop means the first failing cancel skips all remaining reminders including already-cancelled ones, which retry forever

immediateDelete path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels SendGrid but returns without deleting the DB row, leaving orphaned WorkflowReminder rows with scheduled: true that phantom-appear in scheduled-reminder queries on reschedule paths

Cancellation query semantics defer actual SendGrid cancel to an hourly cron with a one-hour grace period, so attendees can still receive emails for cancelled bookings between cancellation and cron run, with no fallback deadline; SMS and email channels have divergent cancellation semantics for the same user action

The cancelled column on WorkflowReminder is method-dependent (only applies to email reminders; SMS rows are deleted immediately), so its meaning is ambiguous for future callers and would benefit from a named separation or CancellationState enum

Gating condition in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, making the sender-id configuration UI unreachable when only isSenderIdNeeded is true even though the boolean and its actions still exist

try/catch around forEach with async callbacks in handleNewBooking.ts (and workflows.tsx) cannot catch anything since the async calls are not awaited, so cancellation failures appear logged but are silently discarded

Cancellation of booking/reschedule leaves email reminders as permanent cancelled:true rows in DB unless immediateDelete passed; old SendGrid DELETE scheduled_sends call was dropped and lifecycle contract changed silently (emailReminderManager.ts:197-230)

Refactored reminder deletion loop lost ownership scoping; deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder delete by bare id with no user check, allowing deletion of another user's scheduled reminders (workflows.tsx:372-380)

Condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, so sender-ID input area no longer renders when only isSenderIdNeeded is true (WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390)

forEach wrapping non-awaited async delete calls means catch is dead code and cancellations race with booking update; Prisma rejections become unhandled and failures silently defeat reminder cancellation on reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:964-975)

scheduleEmailReminders cron sweep only cleans cancelled reminders within 1 hour of scheduledDate; reminders further out are never cancelled or deleted, with behavior differing by caller path and no documented rationale for the 1-hour threshold (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-48)

deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder perform prisma.workflowReminder.delete with no user/tenant scope, removing the ownership check that previously backstopped deletion — creating a bare-id delete primitive vulnerable to future IDOR

remindersToCancel query in scheduleEmailReminders.ts omits the scheduled: true condition, allowing non-scheduled cancelled rows (with null referenceId) to enter the loop and issue null batch_id requests to SendGrid

A poison-pill row with no referenceId throws during SendGrid cancellation and aborts the try block, blocking deletion of other legitimately cancelled reminders and leaving earlier rows cancelled at the provider but not purged from the DB
console.log of SDK error objects at scheduleEmailReminders.ts:68 can leak request URLs, headers, and response bodies (account identifiers, auth-adjacent material) into unredacted server logs

No test code added anywhere in the diff despite substantive behavioral changes (new cancelled soft-delete state machine, reminder-cancellation sweep, cancellation-on-reschedule, isPhoneNumberNeeded restructure)

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:49-77 cancellation sweep is unverifiable by tests: the try/catch wraps both SendGrid cancellation and Prisma deletes, swallows errors, and returns success regardless of partial vs full cancellation
A SendGrid API error mid-loop leaves the DB in a half-cancelled, half-pending state where the cancelled flag and DB rows diverge, which the next run will re-attempt
Error-handling contract is 'swallow and log to console', making regression tests asserting cancellation correctness impossible without inspecting console output
Tombstone rows with cancelled=true are cascade-deleted before the cron reader can consume them, so superseded scheduled SendGrid emails for rescheduled bookings still fire
Asymmetric cancel semantics: SMS reminders get no tombstone or retry path, and a single Twilio API failure silently swallows the cancel leaving the reminder row active with no trace of cancel attempt
remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fire-and-forget deletes are never awaited, reintroducing a race with subsequent re-scheduling logic that can read stale not-yet-deleted reminder rows
Cron consumer permanently deletes WorkflowReminder rows for cancelled reminders, destroying the audit record needed to diagnose or retry failed SendGrid cancels

deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps twilio.cancelSMS and prisma delete in a try/catch that only console.logs, so if Twilio cancel fails both the remote cancel and row delete are skipped, leaving reminder scheduled:true with no retry or cleanup for SMS, causing the attendee to still receive the SMS for a cancelled booking

remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) in workflows.tsx is never awaited (no Promise.all), so the tRPC mutation returns success before SendGrid cancels and cancelled:true updates execute, risking stranded reminders on serverless cold-start freeze
Same unawaited forEach pattern at workflows.tsx:211-216 (delete) and :517-522 (deleted step)

handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings.tsx invoke deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder in forEach without await, so the cancel/reschedule API resolves before remote cancellation, allowing reminders to still fire after a successful API response

handleNewBooking.ts try/catch around forEach of deleteScheduledEmailReminder is dead code: the forEach body is synchronous and managers swallow their own errors, so the catch is unreachable and failures are never retried or surfaced

scheduleEmailReminders.ts cleanup loop awaits client.request per reminder sequentially with no timeout in a single try/catch that only logs; a failure or hang on reminder N aborts the loop leaving later reminders not cancelled at SendGrid until a subsequent run
scheduleEmailReminders.ts where clause filters only on cancelled:true and scheduledDate, not on scheduled or method, so any such row is blindly POSTed to SendGrid's scheduled_sends endpoint

scheduleEmailReminders.ts calls client.request with batch_id: null if a cancelled reminder has referenceId null, causing SendGrid error, logged catch, and loop abort that silently drops all subsequent legitimate cancellations in that run; needs a null-check before the request

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts the try/catch wraps synchronous forEach over fire-and-forget async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls, so the catch is dead code and rejections become unhandled promise rejections

In workflows.tsx the async callback inside remindersToUpdate.forEach is not awaited, so the mutation proceeds before deletes complete, causing rescheduling while old reminders are still being deleted with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff shows `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); });` where the callback is `async` but the `forEach` is not awaited, and the async cancellation functions are invoked without `await`. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async (they hit Prisma and external APIs per this diff), the surrounding mutation will continue before these cancellations/deletes finish, allowing subsequent logic (e.g., updating steps/reminders) to run while old reminders are still being cancelled/deleted, with any errors potentially unobserved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Changing deleteMany to delete in emailReminderManager.ts/smsReminderManager.ts throws P2025 on double invocation (cancelled-then-rescheduled bookings flow through both handlers), causing the subsequent SendGrid/Twilio cancel to silently fail and reminders to stay live

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `deleteMany` to `delete` for SMS reminders (`smsReminderManager.ts`), but the claimed failure mode (“P2025 on double invocation causes subsequent SendGrid/Twilio cancel to silently fail and reminders stay live”) is not supported by the code shown. In `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, the Twilio cancel (`twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)`) happens *before* the Prisma `delete`, so even if a second invocation hits P2025, the external cancel was already attempted. For email, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` no longer deletes the row in the normal path; it updates `cancelled: true` (no P2025), and the actual SendGrid cancel+delete is performed later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` based on `cancelled=true`. The only email path that does a DB delete is when `referenceId` is null, in which case there is no SendGrid cancel to fail. Thus the finding’s causal chain (P2025 => cancel not executed => reminders remain live) is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The event-type disable path in workflows.tsx removed ownership scoping (userId check) from reminder deletion, allowing users to cancel and delete other users' scheduled reminders

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` (event-type disable path), the diff removes the explicit ownership constraint `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` that previously guarded reminder deletion (`ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)`). It now iterates `remindersToDelete` and calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, ...)`, and those managers perform `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete` by `id` only (no `userId`/booking scoping). This is a loss of defense-in-depth and could become an authorization bug if the earlier `remindersToDelete` query is ever insufficiently scoped, but the diff alone doesn’t prove that other users’ reminders can be reached via this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sweep in scheduleEmailReminders.ts doesn't check scheduled or referenceId, so a cancelled reminder with null referenceId issues a SendGrid request with null batch_id that fails, aborting deletion of that reminder and all subsequent ones since Promise.all never runs

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new sweep queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` and then unconditionally does a SendGrid cancel request with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. There is no guard for `referenceId` being null/undefined. If any `cancelled` reminder has a null `referenceId`, `client.request` will be called with `batch_id: null`, likely throwing and jumping to the surrounding `catch`, which prevents queuing any Prisma deletes and skips the final `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, leaving that reminder (and any subsequent ones) undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WorkflowStepContainer.tsx removed the isSenderIdNeeded render branch but kept the variable, losing the sender-ID input so SMS workflow steps can't be completed and possibly failing lint

adjudication.rationale: In WorkflowStepContainer.tsx the conditional wrapper changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) && (...)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded && (...)`. This means when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, the entire input section no longer renders (a behavior regression compared to before). The diff does not show whether `isSenderIdNeeded` is still declared/used elsewhere, but it is clearly no longer part of the render condition here.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the new reminder cancellation calls are async but are invoked inside forEach without await, and their returned promises are not collected into prismaPromises (now only [attendeeDeletes, bookingReferenceDeletes]). So the handler can complete (and the cancel response can be sent) before reminder DB updates/deletes finish, leaving rows temporarily (or permanently on failure) with cancelled still false / reminders not fully cancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Diff contains zero tests for any of the new cancellation semantics (immediate SendGrid cancel, deferred cancelled:true + cron sweep, SMS hard delete, new DB column, new cron branch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new cancellation behavior (e.g., `WorkflowReminder.cancelled` column + migration, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now sometimes sets `cancelled: true` instead of cancelling immediately, `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` adds a new branch to sweep `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and then delete them, and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now hard-deletes the reminder). However, the diff shows no accompanying test additions/updates (no test files modified or added) to validate these new semantics across cancel/reschedule paths (`handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts`, TRPC routers). This is a concrete review gap but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cancel branch error handling: if a SendGrid cancel call fails mid-loop, console.log swallows the error and the already-computed deletes are skipped, leaving reminders cancelled:true forever with no retry or cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch`. If any `await client.request(...)` throws mid-loop, control jumps to `catch` where the error is only `console.log`’d, and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached. Because the deletes are only queued (not awaited per-iteration), this can leave already-cancelled reminders in the DB with `cancelled: true` and not deleted, and also prevents processing remaining reminders in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cancel branch in scheduleEmailReminders.ts doesn't filter on method: it selects all cancelled reminders regardless of method and unconditionally calls the SendGrid cancel endpoint, so a non-email reminder gets a bogus SendGrid cancel and its row is deleted without cancelling the SMS, causing the Twilio SMS to still fire

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cron cancel branch queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { ... }}})` with no `method` constraint, then for *each* reminder calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel endpoint and then deletes the row (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). Since `WorkflowReminder` can represent both EMAIL and SMS (see `WorkflowMethods` usage elsewhere in the diff), this would wrongly process cancelled SMS reminders via SendGrid and potentially delete them without invoking `twilio.cancelSMS`, allowing an SMS to still fire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reschedule path has no handling for reschedule failure: old booking's reminders are cancelled before eventManager.reschedule runs, so if rescheduling throws, the attendee keeps the old time slot but receives no reminders with no rollback or post-success guard

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, when `originalRescheduledBooking?.uid` is truthy, the code cancels the previous booking’s workflow reminders inside a `try` block **before** calling `eventManager.reschedule(evt, ...)` (see the new block around `// cancel workflow reminders from previous rescheduled booking`). If `eventManager.reschedule` throws, the catch only logs and does not restore reminders or guard cancellation to occur only after a successful reschedule. Also, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` deletes the reminder DB row unconditionally, making rollback impossible from this path. This matches the finding: old booking can remain but its reminders are gone.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, the previous logic always queued a Prisma deleteMany for every workflowReminder row, regardless of method. The new code only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...) inside EMAIL/SMS branches and performs no fallback deletion/update for other reminder.method values. If WorkflowMethods can include values beyond EMAIL/SMS, those reminders would now be skipped and their DB rows would persist on cancellation, whereas they were previously deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 changes wrapper condition from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, silently removing sender-ID panel rendering — an unscoped user-visible behavior change

adjudication.rationale: In `WorkflowStepContainer.tsx`, the wrapper render condition is changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to only `isPhoneNumberNeeded`. The diff shows no alternative UI path for the `isSenderIdNeeded` case, so when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, the entire panel that previously rendered will no longer render—an unscoped, user-visible behavior change likely breaking sender-id-related configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts sweeps all cancelled:true reminders globally with no user or method filter, giving email a soft-cancel lifecycle while deleteScheduledSMSReminder (smsReminderManager.ts:177) hard-deletes rows immediately — undeclared asymmetric design across transports

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new sweep queries `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `method: EMAIL` (or `referenceId != null`) filter, then unconditionally calls the email scheduled-send cancel API with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` and deletes the row. Since `WorkflowReminder` rows can be SMS as well (see `WorkflowMethods` usage elsewhere in the diff), this code can attempt to cancel SMS reminders via the email provider API (and/or pass a null `referenceId`), which is a real correctness defect introduced by the change. The noted email soft-cancel vs SMS hard-delete asymmetry is also present in the diff (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now sets `cancelled=true` unless `immediateDelete`, while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` deletes immediately), but the missing method/referenceId filtering in the email sweep is itself a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Call sites (handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking) must know which cancellation semantics to invoke, e.g. immediateDelete is only ever passed for email, baking transport-specific policy into cross-cutting call sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two different cancellation behaviors for email reminders via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`: (1) default path marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (no provider cancel) and relies on `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` to later cancel+delete reminders within the next hour; (2) `immediateDelete=true` triggers an immediate provider cancel request and returns early (no DB delete/update in that function). Multiple cross-cutting call sites now must choose which semantic to apply (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx` call without the flag, while `handleNewBooking.ts` and parts of `workflows.tsx` pass `true`). SMS cancellation has different semantics (`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` always deletes the DB record). This is a diff-grounded architecture/policy coupling concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete third parameter on deleteScheduledEmailReminder leaks call-site-specific policy into a shared manager, giving it contradictory semantics with no documented requirement mapping

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` was changed from a single-purpose canceller to a multi-behavior function controlled by an `immediateDelete?: boolean` flag (emailReminderManager.ts). With `immediateDelete` it calls the external cancel API and returns early; without it, it merely marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (and doesn’t contact the provider), and if `referenceId` is null it hard-deletes the DB row. Call sites now pass `true` only in some contexts (e.g., workflows router delete/step delete, handleNewBooking reschedule), while other contexts omit it. This is a diff-grounded API/semantics concern: a shared “manager” now encodes call-site policy via a boolean, and the name `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` no longer consistently maps to what it does (cancel now vs mark-cancelled vs delete row), which makes the behavior harder to reason about and maintain even if it may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:965 uses immediateDelete: true for email but the paired SMS call has no equivalent — same lifecycle event gets opposite persistence semantics per transport

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the reschedule cleanup calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) but calls deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) with no equivalent option. Per the diff, deleteScheduledSMSReminder always deletes the WorkflowReminder row (and cancels Twilio if referenceId exists), while deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true only cancels the external scheduled send and then returns early without deleting or even marking the DB reminder as cancelled. That creates inconsistent persistence/cleanup semantics for the same lifecycle event and can leave orphaned email reminders in the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx:572-580 deletion moved into shared managers that delete by bare id with no ownership check, losing the user-scoping clause (booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }) and introducing an authorization regression

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the prior DB deletion used `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` (user-scoped). The diff replaces that with calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`. The shared managers then perform `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` (SMS) or `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` (Email) with no ownership/user scoping. This removes the explicit authorization guard present before and can allow deleting/updating a reminder solely by ID if an out-of-scope ID is ever reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: schema.prisma cancelled Boolean? column is nullable with no default and no code writes false, introducing a NULL third state that future queries like cancelled: false will silently miss
matched_golden_ids: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that `cancelled` is nullable (`Boolean?`) with no default, creating a NULL third state so records may not be treated as `false` and queries/checks like `cancelled: false` can miss them—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls in handleCancelBooking.ts (and bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) are un-awaited inside forEach with the previous Promise.all guarantee removed, so cancellation never completes in serverless environments, causing cancelled bookings to still send reminders and reminder rows to leak

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places the diff replaces explicit Prisma deletion Promise collection/awaiting with fire-and-forget calls to async reminder cancellation functions, without awaiting them. Example: `handleCancelBooking.ts` removed `remindersToDelete` and removed it from `prismaPromises`, but now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` inside `forEach` with no `await` and no later `Promise.all`. Same pattern occurs in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (removed `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`) and in several loops in `workflows.tsx`. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and now also perform Prisma writes (`update`/`delete`), not awaiting them means cancellation/DB updates can be dropped before the request finishes (notably in serverless), leaving reminders still active and/or `WorkflowReminder` rows not cleaned up/marked cancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteScheduledEmailReminder swallows all errors with console.log and returns normally, so combined with un-awaited calls there is no path to detect failed SendGrid cancels, meaning reminders for every cancelled booking are sent forever with no signal

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` wraps all logic in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and does not rethrow, so callers cannot detect failure. Multiple call sites invoke it inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `workflows.tsx`, `handleNewBooking.ts`), meaning the request can complete with no guarantee the SendGrid cancel (or even the Prisma `update/delete`) succeeded. If the cancel/update fails, reminders can still be sent for cancelled/rescheduled bookings with no signal to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sequential per-reminder SendGrid API calls in scheduleEmailReminders.ts cron loop cause N+1 external calls, and a single try/catch around the loop means the first failing cancel skips all remaining reminders including already-cancelled ones, which retry forever

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block does `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)) }` inside a single outer `try/catch`. This makes SendGrid cancel calls sequential (N external calls) and, more importantly, if any `client.request` throws, control jumps to the `catch` and the loop stops and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is skipped. That leaves remaining reminders unprocessed, and can also leave earlier reminders (already successfully canceled via SendGrid) still in the DB because their deletes were only queued, causing them to be picked up again on the next cron run (`cancelled: true` + `scheduledDate <= ...`) and retried indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels SendGrid but returns without deleting the DB row, leaving orphaned WorkflowReminder rows with scheduled: true that phantom-appear in scheduled-reminder queries on reschedule paths

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early on the `immediateDelete` path after canceling SendGrid (POST cancel) and does not delete or update the `WorkflowReminder` row (`return;` before any Prisma call). Multiple call sites in the diff removed their own `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` cleanup and now rely on this function (e.g., `workflows.tsx` uses `immediateDelete: true` when deleting workflows/steps; `handleNewBooking.ts` uses `immediateDelete: true` on reschedule). This leaves DB rows behind, and because the `cancelled` flag is not set in the `immediateDelete` branch, the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which only processes `cancelled: true`) won’t remove them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cancellation query semantics defer actual SendGrid cancel to an hourly cron with a one-hour grace period, so attendees can still receive emails for cancelled bookings between cancellation and cron run, with no fallback deadline; SMS and email channels have divergent cancellation semantics for the same user action

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation to often *not* cancel the upstream SendGrid scheduled send immediately. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now, by default, only sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true` in Prisma and returns (no SendGrid API cancel/delete), unless `immediateDelete` is passed or `referenceId` is null. Call sites for booking cancellation/reschedule (`handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, parts of `viewer/workflows.tsx`) mostly call it without `immediateDelete`, so SendGrid jobs can remain active. Actual SendGrid cancellation is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only cancels reminders where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a verifiable window where a cancelled/rescheduled booking’s email could still be sent if the cancellation job doesn’t run before the scheduled send time. Meanwhile SMS cancellation (`deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) still attempts immediate Twilio cancellation and deletes the DB record, so the channels have divergent cancellation semantics for the same user action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The cancelled column on WorkflowReminder is method-dependent (only applies to email reminders; SMS rows are deleted immediately), so its meaning is ambiguous for future callers and would benefit from a named separation or CancellationState enum

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled Boolean?` to `WorkflowReminder` and uses it only in the email cancellation path: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (when not `immediateDelete`) while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` deletes the row outright. Additionally, `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, ... }})` and then cancels/deletes those reminders via the email provider. There is no analogous use of `cancelled` for SMS. This makes the semantic meaning of `cancelled` method-dependent and potentially confusing for future callers, matching the finding as an architectural/clarity concern rather than a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gating condition in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, making the sender-id configuration UI unreachable when only isSenderIdNeeded is true even though the boolean and its actions still exist

adjudication.rationale: In `WorkflowStepContainer.tsx`, the conditional wrapper was changed from `{(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) && (...)}` to `{isPhoneNumberNeeded && (...)}`. This is verifiable in the diff and means the entire configuration block will no longer render when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, making any sender-id-only UI that previously relied on that wrapper unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: try/catch around forEach with async callbacks in handleNewBooking.ts (and workflows.tsx) cannot catch anything since the async calls are not awaited, so cancellation failures appear logged but are silently discarded

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new cancellation logic wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a try/catch, but the body calls async functions (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`) without `await`. Any promise rejection would not be caught by the surrounding try/catch, and the handler proceeds immediately to `eventManager.reschedule(...)` without waiting for reminder cancellation to complete. Similarly in workflows.tsx multiple places switched from collecting Prisma promises + `await Promise.all(...)` to plain `forEach` (and even `forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` at ~586) without awaiting, so reminder cancellation/deletion may race with subsequent workflow updates and failures won't be surfaced to callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cancellation of booking/reschedule leaves email reminders as permanent cancelled:true rows in DB unless immediateDelete passed; old SendGrid DELETE scheduled_sends call was dropped and lifecycle contract changed silently (emailReminderManager.ts:197-230)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now marks DB rows `cancelled: true` (non-immediate path) instead of deleting them immediately, but `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` adds a cleanup pass that finds `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true` (and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`), cancels the SendGrid batch, and then deletes the reminder rows. So the claim that cancellation/reschedule leaves reminders as “permanent cancelled:true rows” is not supported by the diff. While the lifecycle contract does change (DB flag + later cleanup instead of immediate SendGrid cancel+delete), permanence is contradicted by the added deletion logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Refactored reminder deletion loop lost ownership scoping; deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder delete by bare id with no user check, allowing deletion of another user's scheduled reminders (workflows.tsx:372-380)

adjudication.rationale: In workflows router, the old code deleted reminders via `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` (scoped to the current user). The refactor replaces this with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (workflows.tsx ~372+). Those helper functions now perform `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` / `update({ where: { id: reminderId }})` with no user/booking ownership condition. That is an authorization/tenant-isolation regression compared to the previous scoped delete and could allow deleting another user’s reminder if an unscoped/incorrect reminder id enters the set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, so sender-ID input area no longer renders when only isSenderIdNeeded is true (WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390)

adjudication.rationale: In WorkflowStepContainer.tsx the render guard was changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` only. This means when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, the entire input panel that previously would render will no longer render at all, which matches the finding’s claim of lost UI in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: forEach wrapping non-awaited async delete calls means catch is dead code and cancellations race with booking update; Prisma rejections become unhandled and failures silently defeat reminder cancellation on reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:964-975)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new reschedule cleanup wraps a workflowReminders.forEach() in try/catch but calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...) without awaiting. Those functions are async (return Promises), so any rejection will not be caught by the surrounding try/catch, potentially becoming unhandled, and cancellation work can race with subsequent reschedule logic. This matches the finding and is directly shown in the diff (handleNewBooking.ts ~950-975 plus async delete* definitions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders cron sweep only cleans cancelled reminders within 1 hour of scheduledDate; reminders further out are never cancelled or deleted, with behavior differing by caller path and no documented rationale for the 1-hour threshold (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-48)

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new sweep only selects cancelled reminders with `scheduledDate.lte(dayjs().add(1, "hour"))` and then cancels/deletes them. Cancelled email reminders outside that window are intentionally left in DB with `cancelled: true` (set by `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` when `immediateDelete` is not passed) and will only be picked up later as they fall within the 1-hour window. So the finding’s “never cancelled or deleted” claim isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff, but the 1-hour cutoff and differing caller behavior (`immediateDelete` true vs. flagging) are real, diff-grounded design/edge-case concerns that should be documented/justified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder perform prisma.workflowReminder.delete with no user/tenant scope, removing the ownership check that previously backstopped deletion — creating a bare-id delete primitive vulnerable to future IDOR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a bare-id delete primitive: smsReminderManager.deleteScheduledSMSReminder now does `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`, and emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder can `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` when `referenceId` is null. In several call sites (e.g. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`), the previous scoped `deleteMany` that included `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` was removed and replaced with these helpers, so the defense-in-depth ownership/tenant check is indeed gone. However, from the diff alone, the helper is only called with `reminder.id` values fetched by server-side queries (not user-supplied IDs), so an actual IDOR exploit is not directly verifiable here; it’s a real security-hardening/regression concern created by the change rather than a provable defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remindersToCancel query in scheduleEmailReminders.ts omits the scheduled: true condition, allowing non-scheduled cancelled rows (with null referenceId) to enter the loop and issue null batch_id requests to SendGrid

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `remindersToCancel` is fetched with only `{ cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` and then the loop unconditionally issues a SendGrid cancel request with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. Since `referenceId` is nullable (`string | null` elsewhere in the diff) and the query does not constrain to scheduled/email reminders, a cancelled row with `referenceId = null` (or even a non-email reminder) would result in an invalid SendGrid request (`batch_id: null`) / wrong-provider cancellation attempt. The missing `scheduled: true` (and/or `referenceId != null`, `method == EMAIL`) filter or a null-guard is a correctness issue in the added cancellation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A poison-pill row with no referenceId throws during SendGrid cancellation and aborts the try block, blocking deletion of other legitimately cancelled reminders and leaving earlier rows cancelled at the provider but not purged from the DB

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block iterates `remindersToCancel` inside a single `try { for (...) { await client.request(... batch_id: reminder.referenceId ...) ... } await Promise.all(...) } catch { ... }`. If any cancelled reminder row has `referenceId` null/undefined, the SendGrid `client.request` call will likely throw, immediately jumping to the `catch` and skipping both the remaining reminders and the final `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. Because deletions are only enqueued (not awaited) before the throw, earlier reminders may already be cancelled at the provider (due to the preceding `await client.request`) but not purged from the DB, and later valid reminders won’t be processed at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: console.log of SDK error objects at scheduleEmailReminders.ts:68 can leak request URLs, headers, and response bodies (account identifiers, auth-adjacent material) into unredacted server logs

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the newly added catch block logs the caught SDK error via `console.log(`Error cancelling scheduled Emails: ${error}`);`. Since the code is making `client.request(...)` calls, the thrown `error` can be an SDK/http error object that may include request/response details (potentially URLs, headers, bodies, identifiers). Logging it unredacted to server logs is a security/privacy defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test code added anywhere in the diff despite substantive behavioral changes (new cancelled soft-delete state machine, reminder-cancellation sweep, cancellation-on-reschedule, isPhoneNumberNeeded restructure)

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes substantial behavioral changes (adds `cancelled` state on `WorkflowReminder`, changes cancellation behavior in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, adds a cancellation sweep in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, cancels reminders on reschedule in `handleNewBooking.ts`, and restructures `isPhoneNumberNeeded` UI logic), but no test files or test cases are added/updated anywhere in the shown diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap for newly introduced nontrivial logic rather than a generic request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:49-77 cancellation sweep is unverifiable by tests: the try/catch wraps both SendGrid cancellation and Prisma deletes, swallows errors, and returns success regardless of partial vs full cancellation

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the newly added cancellation sweep wraps both the SendGrid cancel request and the Prisma delete loop in a single try/catch, and on any error it only console.logs and then continues on to the rest of the handler (no rethrow / no response signaling). This makes partial vs. full cancellation non-observable and hard to verify, and failures will be silently ignored by the endpoint’s caller/cron even though cancellations/deletes may not have completed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A SendGrid API error mid-loop leaves the DB in a half-cancelled, half-pending state where the cancelled flag and DB rows diverge, which the next run will re-attempt

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, cancellation is done in a single `try` that loops `remindersToCancel`. Each iteration `await`s the SendGrid cancel request, but only *collects* Prisma `delete()` promises and runs `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop. If a SendGrid error throws mid-loop, control jumps to `catch` before `Promise.all`, so reminders successfully cancelled in SendGrid earlier in the loop will not have their DB rows deleted. On the next run they will be selected again by `findMany({ cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }})` and re-attempted, leaving the DB and external state out of sync until a fully successful run occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error-handling contract is 'swallow and log to console', making regression tests asserting cancellation correctness impossible without inspecting console output

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/continues a pattern where reminder-cancellation failures are caught and only logged, with no error propagation or structured result returned. Examples: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` both `catch` and `console.log(...)` without rethrowing; `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` wraps cancellation/deletion in a `try/catch` and only `console.log` on failure; `handleNewBooking.ts` cancellation is wrapped in `try/catch` and logs via `log.error` but continues. This makes it hard for callers/tests to deterministically assert cancellation correctness because failures do not surface through return values/exceptions, only via logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tombstone rows with cancelled=true are cascade-deleted before the cron reader can consume them, so superseded scheduled SendGrid emails for rescheduled bookings still fire

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cancelled` flag on `WorkflowReminder` and changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to usually *update* the reminder row (`cancelled: true`) instead of deleting it (unless `!referenceId`, or `immediateDelete` where it cancels via API and returns). Call sites for rescheduling/cancelling bookings also removed the previous `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` logic, so the reminders are generally no longer cascade-removed by this code. The new cron/API (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts`) explicitly queries `cancelled: true` reminders and cancels+deletes them. Nothing in the shown diff indicates that `cancelled=true` rows are being cascade-deleted before that reader can see them, nor that this would cause rescheduled SendGrid emails to still fire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric cancel semantics: SMS reminders get no tombstone or retry path, and a single Twilio API failure silently swallows the cancel leaving the reminder row active with no trace of cancel attempt

adjudication.rationale: In `smsReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` wraps both the Twilio cancel call and the Prisma delete in a single `try` block. If `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, the catch runs and the DB row is **not deleted** (and there is no `cancelled` tombstone update like email uses in `emailReminderManager.ts`). Since call sites in this diff removed their separate `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` cleanup (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, `viewer/workflows.tsx`), a single Twilio API failure can now leave the reminder row present/active with only a console log and no retry/cancel state persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fire-and-forget deletes are never awaited, reintroducing a race with subsequent re-scheduling logic that can read stale not-yet-deleted reminder rows

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff introduces `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); });` without collecting/awaiting the resulting promises. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async (they hit external APIs and/or update/delete `workflowReminder` rows), this becomes fire-and-forget and subsequent logic in the same handler can run before the reminder cancellation/update completes, allowing stale reminder rows/state to be observed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron consumer permanently deletes WorkflowReminder rows for cancelled reminders, destroying the audit record needed to diagnose or retry failed SendGrid cancels

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cron-like handler explicitly deletes `WorkflowReminder` rows after attempting to cancel them (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } })` for each reminder found with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`). That does permanently remove cancelled reminders from the DB, which could eliminate any long-term audit/history of what was cancelled. However, the finding’s implication about preventing retries for failed cancels isn’t strictly supported: if the SendGrid cancel request throws, the delete is not executed and the reminder remains for a future run. This reads more like a data-retention/observability concern than a clearly incorrect behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps twilio.cancelSMS and prisma delete in a try/catch that only console.logs, so if Twilio cancel fails both the remote cancel and row delete are skipped, leaving reminder scheduled:true with no retry or cleanup for SMS, causing the attendee to still receive the SMS for a cancelled booking

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` does `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and then `await prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` inside a single `try`. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, control jumps to the `catch` and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the reminder row intact (no `cancelled` flag set for SMS either) and no retry/cleanup mechanism shown in this diff. This can result in SMS reminders not being properly cancelled/cleaned up when cancellation fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) in workflows.tsx is never awaited (no Promise.all), so the tRPC mutation returns success before SendGrid cancels and cancelled:true updates execute, risking stranded reminders on serverless cold-start freeze

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff introduces `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); });` with no `await` on the async reminder-manager calls and no aggregation/`Promise.all` for the loop. Because `forEach` doesn’t await and the callback itself doesn’t await the returned promises, the mutation can proceed/return before the reminder cancellation DB updates (`cancelled: true` in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`) or deletes (`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` deletes the row) have completed, leaving work in-flight/unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same unawaited forEach pattern at workflows.tsx:211-216 (delete) and :517-522 (deleted step)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff shows multiple `forEach` loops that call async cancellation functions without awaiting their returned promises. Examples:
- Around `scheduledReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` (near the `//cancel workflow reminders of deleted workflow` comment). Both `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are `async` (see their definitions in this diff) and perform network/DB work, but the router does not await them.
- Similarly in the deleted-step path: `remindersFromStep.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })`.
Because these are not awaited, the TRPC procedure can continue/return while cancellations/DB updates are still in flight, and any errors will be unobserved—risking reminders not being cancelled/deleted consistently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings.tsx invoke deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder in forEach without await, so the cancel/reschedule API resolves before remote cancellation, allowing reminders to still fire after a successful API response

adjudication.rationale: In both `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the diff changes reminder cleanup to call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without `await` and without collecting the returned promises into the `Promise.all(...)` that gates the API completion. The called functions are `async` (see `emailReminderManager.ts` and `smsReminderManager.ts`), so the handler/router can resolve and return a success response before the cancellation DB update/delete (and/or remote cancellation) completes, which can allow reminders to still run after a successful cancel/reschedule response, especially in serverless environments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts try/catch around forEach of deleteScheduledEmailReminder is dead code: the forEach body is synchronous and managers swallow their own errors, so the catch is unreachable and failures are never retried or surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new try/catch wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)`, but the loop does not `await` the async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` calls. Separately, both managers shown in the diff catch and only `console.log` errors (no rethrow), so failures from those async operations won’t be surfaced to this try/catch anyway. The catch isn’t strictly “unreachable” (a synchronous error inside the loop could still throw), but as written it provides little/no error handling for the async cancellations and doesn’t enable retries or propagation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts cleanup loop awaits client.request per reminder sequentially with no timeout in a single try/catch that only logs; a failure or hang on reminder N aborts the loop leaving later reminders not cancelled at SendGrid until a subsequent run

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block wraps the entire cleanup in a single try/catch and performs `await client.request(...)` inside a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop. If the SendGrid cancel request throws (or never resolves) on reminder N, execution jumps to the catch and the loop stops, so later reminders in `remindersToCancel` are not cancelled/deleted in that run. No timeout/abort mechanism is shown for `client.request`, so a hang would also block the whole handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts where clause filters only on cancelled:true and scheduledDate, not on scheduled or method, so any such row is blindly POSTed to SendGrid's scheduled_sends endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new `remindersToCancel` query filters only by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, with no constraint on `method` (EMAIL), `scheduled`, or even `referenceId` being non-null. Immediately after, the code iterates all returned reminders and blindly calls SendGrid `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` using `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. If a cancelled reminder is an SMS reminder or has a null/invalid `referenceId`, this will incorrectly hit the SendGrid endpoint (or send a null batch_id) and then delete the DB row, producing broken cancellation behavior and potential data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts calls client.request with batch_id: null if a cancelled reminder has referenceId null, causing SendGrid error, logged catch, and loop abort that silently drops all subsequent legitimate cancellations in that run; needs a null-check before the request

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, remindersToCancel is fetched solely by { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } with no filter ensuring referenceId is non-null. The subsequent loop unconditionally does client.request({ body: { batch_id: reminder.referenceId, status: "cancel" } }), so a reminder with referenceId === null will send batch_id: null and likely throw. Because the try/catch wraps the entire loop, the first such error aborts the rest of the cancellations for that run (only logs in catch), matching the finding; a null-check (or query filter) is needed before calling client.request.
